finding.claim: Broken authorization on DELETE /projects/:id. The handler calls authorized(), which returns a boolean instead of throwing, and discards the result. The ownership/admin check has no effect, so any authenticated user can delete any project. The sibling PUT handler uses authorize(), which throws on failure, so the two handlers are inconsistent.
finding.source: Any authenticated user (req.user) sending DELETE /projects/<victim project id>, where the project is owned by someone else and the caller is not an admin.

trace.note: project is loaded by the attacker-supplied req.params.id with no ownership scoping
authorized(req.user, project) returns false for a non-owner, but the return value is ignored and nothing is thrown
authorized() only computes a boolean (owner or admin) and has no side effects
the handler returns 204, so the attacker sees success

finding.guards_checked: Checked for authorization middleware in this file and found none. Only the router is exported, so any upstream authentication middleware is outside the code under review. authorized() is the only check on this path, and it is ineffective because its result is discarded. There is no try/catch or throw on the failure path. No other ownership scoping applies, since the store lookup is by id only.

verdict.guard_found: authorized() at api.js:12-14 is a boolean-returning function whose result is discarded at api.js:18. Nothing throws, and there is no try/catch, middleware or ownership scoping in this file. The authorize() that throws (api.js:4-10) is only used by the PUT handler at api.js:25.
verdict.reason: At api.js:18 the boolean from authorized() (defined at api.js:12-14) is dropped, so api.js:19 deletes the project for any authenticated non-owner, unlike the PUT handler, which calls the throwing authorize() at api.js:25. The one gap is that upstream authentication middleware is not visible in this file, but the attacker only needs to be an ordinary logged-in user.

verdict_facts.guard_found: authorized() at api.js:12-14 returns a boolean and is called as a bare statement at api.js:18, so its result is discarded. No middleware, try/catch or throw guards the DELETE route. The throwing authorize() at api.js:4 is used only by the PUT handler at api.js:25.
verdict_facts.reason: api.js:18 calls the boolean-returning authorized() and ignores the result, so api.js:19 deletes any project for any authenticated user. The other trace lines (17, 12, 19, 20) match the code.
